study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter observational obstetric cohort
outcome: Maternal morbidity (death, hysterectomy, ICU admission, transfusion, unanticipated procedure for bleeding)
Time from delivery to first uterotonic dose
cohort: 7,917 women who experienced postpartum hemorrhage after singleton or twin births from a cohort of over 115,000 mother-neonate pairs from 25 hospitals
finding: The study found that nighttime delivery was not associated with significant differences in postpartum hemorrhage-related management or morbidity compared to daytime delivery.
mod_finding: Women delivering at night were more likely to have a vaginal delivery than those delivering during the day.
